newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.5/9.0 percent on Thursday morning, dealers said.
They said liquidity was ample despite the month-end factor but market operators seemed to be worried over Friday liquidity as tom/next swaps rose to 1.6/1.8 points from 1.2 points.
"It is seldom we have ample supply on a month-end," one foreign bank dealer said.
Dealers said some operators were expecting tighter conditions on Friday due to higher weekly tax payments.
Rises in tom/next swaps drove longer-term swaps up, but longer-term rates in the money market remained relatively low, with one-week money quoted at 13.0 percent.
One Japanese bank dealer said excess supply was due to central bank injection of some 500 billion rupiah.
Dealers said market focus was also on the upcoming public share offering by state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) next week which may cause some tightening in the market.
But some seemed to anticipate stable conditions because the market was not really affected during last year's float of state-owned telecommunications firm Telkom, Indonesia's last large public offer.
"If the money flows into BNI, then it would be tight. But I think most of the money would be kept at present with the underwriters, thus remaining in the market," one trader said.
However, views were mixed as some operators said that the 922 billion rupiah to be raised from the public would inevitably lead to some tightening.
The offer period of BNI is from November 4-7 and the listing will be on November 25.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 0.09 percent against 9.51 percent on Tuesday.
